'''Pablo Prigioni''' (born 17 May 1977) is an Argentine-Italian<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=A2Q |title=ACB.com Pablo Prigioni Varios Doble nacionalidad Argentina-Italia {{in lang{{!}}es}}. |access-date=August 13, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410071854/http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=A2Q |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played the [[point guard]] position,<ref>{{cite web|title=Prigioni, Pablo|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=CBX&seasoncode=E2016|website=www.euroleague.net|access-date=25 April 2018}}</ref> and was a member of the senior [[Argentina national basketball team]] that won the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]]. Prigioni is the oldest rookie in NBA history, making his debut with the [[New York Knicks]] in 2012 at 35. Prior to this, he was a two-time [[All-EuroLeague]] selection playing in Europe, most notably Spain. He played four seasons in the NBA with the Knicks, [[Houston Rockets]], and [[Los Angeles Clippers]] before starting coaching in 2017.

==Professional career==

=== Ramallo (1995–1996) ===
Prigioni began his professional career with Ramallo of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol|Argentine LNB League]] during the 1995–96 season.

=== Belgrano San Nicolás (1996–1998) ===
Prigioni moved to [[Belgrano San Nicolas|Belgrano San Nicolás]] in 1996, playing with them until 1998.

=== Obras Sanitarias (1998–1999) ===
Prigioni transferred to [[Obras Sanitarias]] in 1998 and played with the club until 1999.

=== Fuenlabrada (1999–2001) ===
In 1999, Prigioni moved to the [[Liga ACB|Spanish]] club [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]], where he stayed until 2001.

=== Lucentum Alicante (2001–2003) ===
In 2001, Prigioni joined the Spanish club [[CB Lucentum Alicante|Lucentum Alicante]], and he played there until 2003.

=== Baskonia (2003–2009) ===
In 2003, Prigioni joined the [[EuroLeague]] team [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]]. With Baskonia he won several titles, including: 3 [[Spanish King's Basketball Cup|Spanish King's Cups]] in the years 2004, 2006, 2009; 4 [[Spanish Basketball Supercup|Spanish Supercups]] in the years 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008; and the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] championship in 2008.

=== Real Madrid (2009–2011) ===
In 2009, Prigioni joined [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.baskonia.com/es/noticias_general.asp?id_noticia=2241 |title=Comunicado oficial: Oleson al Caja Laboral; Prigioni y Vidal al Real Madrid |publisher=baskonia.com |date=24 August 2009 |access-date=6 December 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090827100158/http://www.baskonia.com/es/noticias_general.asp?id_noticia=2241 |archive-date=27 August 2009 }}</ref>

=== Return to Baskonia (2011–2012) ===
In August 2011, Prigioni returned to Baskonia, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87269|title=Caja Laboral brings back Prigioni|publisher=EuroLeague|date=August 24, 2011|access-date=December 6, 2016}}</ref>

=== New York Knicks (2012–2015) ===
[[File:Pablo Prigioni NYK 2013.jpg|thumb|right|Prigioni with the [[New York Knicks]] in 2013]]
On July 24, 2012, Prigioni signed a one-year contract with the [[New York Knicks]] for the rookie minimum.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120727083924/http://knicksnow.com/photos/1623/knicks-sign-pablo-prigioni Knicks Sign Pablo Prigioni]</ref> At age 35, Prigioni became the oldest rookie in [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] history, when he made his debut on November 2, 2012. He became the team's starting [[point guard]] for the last two months of the 2012–13 season, as well as for the playoffs. In game 6 of the Knicks' first-round playoff series against the [[Boston Celtics]], Prigioni made 3 three-pointers in the first quarter. The Knicks won 88–80, to advance to the second round of the playoffs for the first time in 13 years.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20130503/NYKBOS/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore Knicks at Celtics, May 3, 2013]</ref>

On July 10, 2013, Prigioni re-signed with the Knicks.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130714081527/http://knicksnow.com/posts/3669/pablo-s-back-knicks-re-sign-the-argentine-point-guard Pablo's Back! Knicks Re-Sign The Argentine Point Guard]</ref>

=== Houston Rockets (2015) ===
On February 19, 2015, Prigioni was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], in exchange for [[Alexey Shved]], and two second-round draft picks.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rockets Acquire K.J. McDaniels and Pablo Prigioni|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-k.j.-mcdaniels-and-pablo-prigioni|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2015–2016) ===
On July 20, 2015, the Rockets traded Prigioni, [[Joey Dorsey]], [[Nick Johnson (basketball)|Nick Johnson]], [[Kostas Papanikolaou]], a 2016 first-round draft pick, and cash considerations, to the [[Denver Nuggets]], in exchange for [[Ty Lawson]] and a 2017 second-round draft pick.<ref name="Lawson trade">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-joey-dorsey-nick-johnson-kostas-papanikolaou-pablo-prigioni-cash-considerations|title=Nuggets Acquire Joey Dorsey, Nick Johnson, Kostas Papanikolaou, Pablo Prigioni, Cash Considerations and First Round Pick From Houston|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2015|access-date=July 20, 2015}}</ref> Prigioni was immediately waived by Denver, upon being acquired.<ref name="Lawson trade" />

On August 3, 2015, Prigioni signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-pablo-prigioni|title=L.A. Clippers sign Pablo Prigioni|work=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2015|access-date=August 5, 2015}}</ref> On January 13, 2016, he had a career-high eight steals against the [[Miami Heat]], which was one shy of the franchise record, held by his head coach, [[Doc Rivers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160113/MIALAC/gameinfo.html|title=Clippers win 10th straight, beat Heat 104-90 without Jordan|work=NBA.com|date=January 13, 2016|access-date=January 14, 2016}}</ref> On April 8, 2016, he recorded a season-high 13 points, a career-high seven rebounds, and a season-high seven assists, in a 102–99 overtime win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/LACUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Crawford scores 30, including winner to lead Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016}}</ref>

On July 29, 2016, Prigioni signed with the Houston Rockets, returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-pablo-prigioni|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Pablo Prigioni|work=NBA.com|date=July 29, 2016|access-date=July 29, 2016}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Rockets on October 24, 2016, after appearing in five preseason games with them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-pablo-prigioni|title=Rockets Waive Pablo Prigioni|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref>

=== Third stint with Baskonia (2016–2017) ===
On December 5, 2016, Prigioni returned to Baskonia, signing with them for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7gbjqoxi6r3hfkug|title=Baskonia brings back legendary playmaker Prigioni|work=EuroLeague.net|publisher=EuroLeague|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> He officially retired from his professional basketball playing career on January 9, 2017.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7j6hywuxprfqe4ma/pablo-prigioni-announces-retirement Pablo Prigioni announces retirement.]</ref><ref>[http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/379463/pablo-prigioni-announces-retirement Pablo Prigioni announces his retirement.]</ref> During his professional career, Prigioni played in 10 EuroLeague seasons, in which he had career averages of 6.1 points, 4.3 assists, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.7 steals per game,<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=CBX&seasoncode=E2016#!careerstats PRIGIONI, PABLO Stats.]</ref> and in four NBA seasons, in which he had career regular season averages of 3.5 points, 2.8 assists, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/prigipa01.html Pablo Prigioni Per Game.]</ref>

On January 15, 2017, following his retirement, Baskonia retired his jersey number 5.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-15 |title=Baskonia retired the jersey of Pablo Prigioni |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/featured/383161/baskonia-retired-jersey-pablo-prigioni/ |access-date=2024-05-07 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

=== Baskonia (2017) ===
On 16 June 2017, Prigioni began his coaching career, when he signed a two-year deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]], to become their new [[head coach]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=EuroLeague.net|date=16 June 2017|access-date=16 June 2017|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7vlls8bb97mehmmw|title=Baskonia names Prigioni new head coach}}</ref> However, on October 26, Prigioni stepped down as Baskonia head coach, after having a 0–3 start in the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|EuroLeague]] and a 2–3 start in the [[2017–18 ACB season|Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Prigioni steps down as Baskonia coach|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8aeqo8kcg7sawu6d|access-date=25 October 2017|work=EuroLeague.net|date=25 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Baskonia, Pablo Prigioni officially part ways|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/spain/acb/251545/baskonia-pablo-prigioni-officially-part-ways.html|access-date=26 October 2017|work=Sportando|date=26 October 2017|language=en}}</ref>

=== Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019) ===
On 24 April 2018, Prigioni joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pablo Prigioni And Tiago Splitter Added To Brooklyn Nets Staff|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/04/24/pablo-prigioni-and-tiago-splitter-added-brooklyn-nets-staff|website=NBA.com|access-date=25 April 2018|date=24 April 2018}}</ref> During the [[2018–19 NBA season]], the Nets returned to the [[NBA playoffs]] for the first time since [[2015 NBA playoffs|2015]].

=== Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–present) ===
On 25 June 2019, Prigioni was hired by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web |last1= |first1= |date=June 25, 2019 |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Name Pablo Prigioni Assistant Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-name-pablo-prigioni-assistant-coach |access-date=7 June 2019 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He coached the Wolves in the 2019 Las Vegas Summer League and was put in charge of the team's offense for the following season.<ref>[https://dunkingwithwolves.com/2019/07/19/3-key-takeaways-from-the-minnesota-timberwolves-at-nba-summer-league/2/ 3 key takeaways from the Minnesota Timberwolves at NBA Summer League]</ref>

=== Argentina (2022–present) ===
On 1 September 2022, Prigioni became the head coach of the [[Argentina men's national basketball team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-01 |title=Pablo Prigioni named coach of the Argentinian national team |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fibawc/1383531/pablo-prigioni-named-coach-of-the-argentinian-national-team/ |access-date=2022-09-01 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
As a member of the [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentine senior men's national basketball team]], Prigioni played at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. He won silver medals at the [[2003 FIBA Americas Championship]] and [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]]. Prigioni was also a member of the Argentina national team that competed at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]] and won the bronze medal. He also won the bronze medal at the [[2009 FIBA Americas Championship]], and the gold medal at the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]].
